May 27 33.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter
No.1520 of May 24, 1933, regarding Tjoeng Khin-fat
(鍾慶發), and to state that this individual was
arrested at 12.15 p.m. May 1, 1933, at No.15 I. Yoen Li,
Carter Road, together with 31 other persons, all of
whom were members of the People's Self-Salvation Associa-
tion to Resist Insult. He was detained on a Writ of
Detention and brought before the Shanghai Special District
Court on May 2 when the case against him was remanded
till May 4. On the latter date he was ordered by the
Court to be released owing to lack of evidence.

A copy of Tjoeng Khin-fat's criminal record
is attached herewith.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your most obedient servant,

Officer i/c Special Branch.

J. Van den Berg, Esq.,
Netherlands Consulate-General.

SHANGHAI, 24th May 1933.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that I would be much obliged to receive some further particulars, if possible, regarding Tjoeng Khin-fat (鍾慶發), a student at the Chinan School, 19 years of age, who on being arrested by the Municipal Police on May the 4th claimed to be a Netherlands' subject, which claim however he could not prove. I would especially like to know whether he was brought before any court and if so on what charge and with what result. I would also like very much to have his fingerprint record in case one has been made.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Proceedings. Mr King S. Kum appeared for the Police.

Mr Kum:- These thirty four accused were arrested on the

and 23rd accused are active communists in the Western District. I
ask that court that they be detained pending the production of ev-
idence, when an application will be made for their handing over.

At 12.25p.m. 1-5-37, D.S.I. Golder, Special Branch, came to Station requesting assistance to raid premises 15 Yi An Li (怡安里), Carter Road, acting upon information which he had received from Communist prisoners, who were arrested earlier during the morning of 1-5-37, by Police from Yulin Road Station, this address supposed to be the Headquarters from whence the Communist Literature was distributed.

D.I. Bennett and party of Police, Uniform and Detectives rendered assistance and these premises were raided.

Thirty seven (37) arrests were effected, a large quantity of literature, supposed Communistic and Anti-Japanese was seized.

Amongst the 37 arrests, 5 males were later identified as being Political agents of the Public Safety Bureau, who were conducting investigations respecting Communistic activities at this address.

All concerned, with the exception of Political agents, (23 males, 9 females) handed over to Yulin Road Station.

Public Safety Bureau agents recognize 9 males and 2 females who were arrested as being involved in Communistic activities.

Proceedings:- Mr. K.S. Kum appeared for the Police.
Mr. Tsai Chi Yung appeared for the Public Safety Bureau.
Mr. Kum:- The Accused were arrested on May 1st. in
the International Settlement, suspected of being Communists.
Application was made by the Police for their detention. During
the remand Period a Representative of the Public Safety Bureau
has identified the Accused as being a communist. This
Representative has brought the necessary witnesses to identify him
in open Court. The Police have no objections to the Accused being
handed over to the Chinese Authorities.
Representative, Dan Oo Tsing:- Some of the witnesses
have surrendered to the P.S.B. and are in Court to identify the
Accused, and as they have not yet been released, I ask that the
case be heard in Camera.
Court cleared by order of the Judge.
Witness, Su Tsung hai:- I was a communist and I
have surrendered to the Public Safety Bureau, where I am now employed
as an assistant detective. I was also arrested in the Settlement
on the 20th. September of last year, and was handed over to the
Chinese Authorities. I had been a communist for 6 years and I
worked in the Western Division of the Communist Group in Shanghai.
I identify Yang Lih Sung as being a communist. Yang was also in the
Shanghai Western Division, and during the Sino-Japanese hostilities
he was in the Three West Provinces, and worked in the 19th. Route
Army. He was also a secretary in the China University.
Accused, Yang Lih Sung:- I do not know this witness.
Prior to the 18th. September 1931 I was in Peking. I am not a
communist, and I think that this witness is greatly mistaken. I only
returned from Peking to Shanghai in last March.
Summing up.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the instructions of Supt. Robertson of Political Branch the four males and two female Chinese arrested by S.I. Verscher at 10.15 a.m. 1/5/33 on North Kiangse Road, appeared before the S.S.D. Court on 2/5/33 on a Writ of Detention for suspected Communistic Activities in the International Settlement and were remanded for one week. The males were ordered to be kept in custody and the females to be allowed to put up security. At the time of arrest these accused had five banners and two separate kinds of pamphlets in their possession. These on being translated were found to be of an Anti-Japanese nature. They stated they got them from 188 Thien Foh Li alleyway Range Road at 10 a.m. 1/5/33 and that they had been delivered at that place at 12 noon 30/4/33 from the Headquarters of the Anti Insult and National Self Salvation League situated at No.15 Yien An Li alleyway off Carter Road. The Range Road address was raided by D.S.I. Golder and party from Political Branch accompanied by the undersigned at 6.40 p.m. 1/5/33 and a quantity of Literature was found and seized. Nothing of a Communistic nature was found on the accused nor at the Thien Foh Li address. The Political Branch has been informed re Court Decision and the undersigned is now waiting instructions from said Branch re further lines of inquiry.

List of communistic literature found in the possession of
Han Lien To (韩连桃), Zan Ching Su (张清苏), Zau How Yeh
(赵厚业), Wong On Yien (黄安贤) and Chiang Kwang Tai
(江光太) who were arrested on Peking Road near Nweichow
Road at 11.35 a.m. May 1, 1933.

1) Pamphlet entitled "Letter to the people protesting
against the fabrication of rumours by the Kuomintang"
purporting to have emanated from the Central Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party dated April 4, 1933.
45 copies.

2) Handbill addressed to the people of Kiangsu in connection
with the fall of Chingwantao, purporting to have emanated
from the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party dated April 20, 1933. (Tobacco Eastern
District).
2 copies.

3) Handbill entitled "Letter of repentance of Li Ming (李明),
a captured divisional commander of the White Army, and
others" dated March 24, 1933".
30 copies.

4) Handbill addressed to the workers and toiling masses in
Kiangsu urging them to protest against the arrest of Lo
Teng Yien (罗登贤) and other revolutionary warriors,
purporting to have emanated from the Kiangsu Provincial
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party dated April 8,
1933.
75 copies.

5) Handbill addressed to the workers on the occupation of
Jehol by the Japanese Imperialists, purporting to have
emanated from the Special District Committee of the
Shanghai Eastern Tobacco District of the Chinese
Communist Party dated March 10.
20 copies.

6) Handbill entitled "Our slogans on the Anniversary of
the International Labour Day - May 1" urging the workers
to commemorate the event by declaring a general strike
and joining the Communist Party.
20 copies.

7) "The Workers' Talk" - May 1 Special Issue - Issue No.1,
dated April 24, 1933, containing articles bearing on the
Anniversary of the International Labour Day - May 1.
10 copies.

8) "Revolutionary Cartoon", Issue No.54 - "April 12" Special
Issue, published by the Pudong Seamen District, containing
drawings urging the workers to commemorate the Anniversary
of April 12.
1 copy.

9) "Revolutionary Cartoon", Issue No.55 - "April 12" Special
Issue, published by the Pudong Seamen District, containing
drawings urging the workers to commemorate the Anniversary
of April 12 by joining the Communist Party, the Old General
Labour Union and the Red Labour Union.
1 copy.

10) Pamphlet entitled "Red May Booklet No.5" containing an
article bearing on the anniversaries during the first month
of Red May, purporting to have emanated from the Propaganda
Section of the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party dated May 1, 1933.
1 copy.

11) Pamphlet entitled "Red May Booklet No.6" containing an
article bearing on the Labour Law promulgated by the
Provisional Central Government of Chinese Soviet in October
1931, purporting to have emanated from the Propaganda Section
of the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist
Party dated May 1.
1 copy.

1933年5月1日上午11时35分，韩连桃（Han Lien To）、张清苏（Zan Ching Su）、赵厚业（Zau How Yeh）、黄安贤（Wong On Yien）和江光太（Chiang Kwang Tai）在北京路近贵州路被捕时，在其身上发现的共产主义文献清单。

1) 小册子，题为《致民众书——抗议国民党制造谣言》，声称出自中国共产党中央委员会，日期为1933年4月4日。
45份。

2) 传单，致江苏民众，涉及秦皇岛失守一事，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会，日期为1933年4月20日。（烟草东区）。
2份。

3) 传单，题为《白军被俘师长李明及其他人的悔过书》，日期为1933年3月24日。
30份。

4) 传单，致江苏工人及劳苦大众，呼吁他们抗议逮捕罗登贤（Lo Teng Yien）及其他革命战士，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会，日期为1933年4月8日。
75份。

5) 传单，致工人，关于日本帝国主义占领热河一事，声称出自中国共产党上海烟草东区特别区委员会，日期为3月10日。
20份。

6) 传单，题为《我们在“五一”国际劳动节纪念日的口号》，呼吁工人通过宣布总罢工和加入共产党来纪念这一节日。
20份。

7) 《工人谈话》——“五一”特刊——第1期，日期为1933年4月24日，包含有关“五一”国际劳动节纪念日的文章。
10份。

8) 《革命漫画》，第54期——“四一二”特刊，由浦东海员区出版，包含呼吁工人纪念“四一二”周年纪念日的画作。
1份。

9) 《革命漫画》，第55期——“四一二”特刊，由浦东海员区出版，包含呼吁工人通过加入共产党、老总工会和红色工会来纪念“四一二”周年纪念日的画作。
1份。

10) 小册子，题为《红五月小册子第5号》，包含有关红五月第一个月期间纪念日的文章，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会宣传部，日期为1933年5月1日。
1份。

11) 小册子，题为《红五月小册子第6号》，包含有关中华苏维埃临时中央政府于1931年10月颁布的劳动法的文章，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会宣传部，日期为5月1日。
1份。
